entities.summary: Gaius Antonius was the second son of Marcus Antonius Creticus and Julia, and thus, younger brother of the Triumvir Mark Antony. Born in 79 BCE, he was a Roman general and politician who played a significant role in the late Roman Republic. Gaius Antonius was a key figure in the Battle of Philippi, where he fought against Octavian and Mark Antony, leading to his eventual death in 41 BCE. His legacy extends to the Roman Empire, with his brother Mark Antony being one of the most influential figures in Roman history. The Antonian dynasty, which ruled Rome from 41 BCE to 37 CE, was a significant period in Roman history, marked by civil wars, political upheaval, and the eventual rise of the Roman Empire. Gaius Antonius' life and legacy are a testament to the complex and tumultuous nature of ancient Roman politics.
